memory.content: Use only OpenAI's official ChatGPT data export. Never scrape ChatGPT, call its internal web endpoints, or run scripts in a chatgpt.com tab, because that likely breaks OpenAI's terms.

Run the migration end to end with minimal human involvement: only ask the user to sign in to ChatGPT once on the box, tap Approve if ChatGPT prompts, and connect an inbox if none is connected. Use defaults instead of questions.
Write the importer locally from the migration skill's spec and pass its acceptance tests before importing the user's real export.

The ChatGPT export-ready email's download link expires 24 hours after it arrives and only works while signed in, so the watcher runs overnight too and downloads it through the signed-in box browser immediately.
Requesting the official ChatGPT export can trigger a phone-approval page that times out within a minute or two; tell the user to approve immediately, and retry once if it lapses.
ChatGPT accounts created with Google sign-in can't be signed in by the box browser automatically; hand the user the screen once to log in, and the session then persists for later downloads.

The official export doesn't include project or custom GPT names and instructions, and its memory snapshots can be stale; read the current memory list, custom instructions and each project's or GPT's page through the signed-in ChatGPT settings UI instead of asking the user.

skills.content:
---
name: ChatGPT to Grok Bot migration
description: >-
  Use when the user wants to move their ChatGPT history (chats, memories, custom
  instructions, projects/GPTs, images and files) into Grok Bot, end to end and
  automatically, using only OpenAI's official data export.
---
# ChatGPT → Grok Bot migration (official export only)

Bring a user's ChatGPT history into Grok Bot using **only OpenAI's official data export**. Never scrape ChatGPT, call its internal web endpoints, or run scripts in a chatgpt.com tab; that likely breaks OpenAI's terms. Write the importer locally from this spec and **pass the acceptance tests** while waiting for the export, then run the rest end to end with minimal human involvement.

## Human steps (keep to these only)
The only things a person must do: (a) sign in to ChatGPT once in the box browser, if it isn't already; (b) tap Approve if ChatGPT sends a phone prompt; (c) connect their inbox connector, if none is connected. Do everything else yourself without asking. Use defaults instead of questions: the user's timezone from their settings, auto-save memories, and auto-create skills.

## 1. Request the official export (bot does it)
- Check the connected inboxes yourself (Gmail/Outlook connectors) and pick the one that receives OpenAI mail. If none is connected, offer the connector once.
- Use a browser subagent to open chatgpt.com in the box browser. If it isn't signed in, hand the screen to the user once to log in (Google sign-in can't be automated), and remind them the login persists for later downloads.
- Go to chatgpt.com/settings/data-controls and click Export, then Confirm export. If a phone-approval page appears, tell the user to tap Approve now and keep the page open about 3 minutes; if it lapses, retry once. Confirm the "Data export requested" banner appears.
- Business/Enterprise workspaces have no self-serve export; tell the user their admin must provide one, then stop. Deleted chats can't be recovered.

## 2. Watch, download and import automatically (routine)
Create a routine in the user's timezone that runs every 30 minutes, including overnight (the link expires 24h after arrival). Each run:
- Search the inbox for OpenAI's export-ready email (read only; never reply). If there isn't one, end silently.
- If it's there, have the signed-in box browser open the link in a new tab and download the zip to `/home/box/Downloads/` (Chrome may add ` (1)`; pick the newest by mtime). Only if it needs a sign-in or approval, tell the user straight away.
- Copy the zip to `raw/`, run the importer, then do step 5 automatically.
- Send the user one summary message, then delete the routine. If 7 days pass with nothing, tell the user and delete the routine.

## 3. Importer to write: `/workspace/chatgpt-import/import_chatgpt.py`
Stdlib only, Python 3.8+. Usage: `import_chatgpt.py <zip-or-dir> --out /workspace/chatgpt-import/archive --tz <user IANA tz>`.

**Export layout:** `conversations.json` (or split `conversations-000.json`, `-001`…), `chat.html`, `user.json`, `message_feedback.json`, `shared_conversations.json`, `model_comparisons.json`. Assets are named `file-<id>-<name>` or sit under `user-*/file_…` and `dalle-generations/`.

**Conversation fields:** `title`, `create_time`, `update_time` (unix float), `mapping` (id→node), `current_node`, `conversation_id`/`id`, optional `gizmo_id` (`g-p-*` = Project, `g-*` = custom GPT), `gizmo_type`, `is_archived`, `is_starred`, `default_model_slug`.

**Node:** `{id, parent, children[], message|null}`. Linearize by walking `parent` from `current_node` to the root, then reverse. Count branches (`children>1`) but render only the current path.

**Message:** `author.role` (system/user/assistant/tool), `create_time`, `content`, `metadata`, `recipient`.

**content_type** (handle every one, never crash):

| type | handling |
|---|---|
| `text` | `parts[]` |
| `multimodal_text` | strings plus `image_asset_pointer` (`asset_pointer`, DALL·E prompt in `metadata.dalle`) or audio |
| `code` | `text`, `language`; a `recipient` starting `canmore.` is a Canvas op: `create_textdoc {name,type,content}`, `update_textdoc {updates:[{pattern,replacement,multiple}]}` |
| `execution_output` | `text`; charts in `metadata.aggregate_result.messages[].image_url` |
| `tether_quote` | quote with url/title |
| `tether_browsing_display` | result/summary |
| `thoughts` | `thoughts[]` |
| `reasoning_recap` | summary |
| `user_editable_context` | custom instructions; harvest, hide from Markdown |
| `model_editable_context` | memory snapshot (`model_set_context`); harvest |
| `system_error` | error text |
| unknown | placeholder |

Hide empty or `is_visually_hidden_from_conversation` messages. Attachments are in `metadata.attachments[{id,name,mimeType}]`.

**Assets:** for `file-service://file-XXX` the id is `file-XXX`; for `sediment://file_000…` the id is `file_…`. Match `/file[-_][A-Za-z0-9]+/` and index files under both spellings. Copy each asset to `assets/<conv id8>/`, put unreferenced files in `assets/_unlinked/`, and list missing ones in `report.json`.

**Outputs under `--out`:**
- `conversations/YYYY/MM/<date>_<slug>_<id8>.md`, with a header of id, title, created/updated in the user's tz, model, project/GPT, archived/starred and branch count.
- `canvases/`, replaying create + update ops into final text.
- `index.csv|json`.
- `archive.sqlite`, with FTS5 `messages_fts` (fall back to LIKE if FTS5 is missing).
- `candidate_facts.md|json`, from custom-instruction and memory snapshots plus heuristic user facts.
- `gizmos.json`, grouping chats by project/GPT id.
- `extras/` (copied side files) and `report.json`.

**Robustness:**
- Re-running merges: dedupe by conversation id, and the newest `update_time` wins.
- Never wipe `--out` unless the user agrees, and never delete files the importer didn't create.
- Wrap each conversation in try/except and record errors in `report.json`.

**Search helper:** `search_archive.py "query" --limit 10` prints title, date, path and snippet for each hit.

## 4. Acceptance tests (must pass before importing real data)
1. `python3 -m py_compile` on both scripts.
2. Build a synthetic official-shaped export: a branched chat, a multimodal image, an attachment, a sediment DALL·E id, code + execution_output chart, a Canvas create/update, user_editable_context, model_editable_context, a project and a GPT chat, a missing file id, an unknown content type, a non-ASCII title, and split `conversations-000/001.json`.
3. Import it and assert:
   - message counts match
   - assets are linked
   - the missing asset is reported
   - the Canvas text contains the update
   - facts are extracted
   - FTS finds a known phrase
   - a second import merges with no duplicates

## 5. After import (automatic)
- **Memory and instructions:** while signed in, use the box browser to read the user's current memory list (Settings → Personalization → Manage memories) and custom instructions. These are a few normal settings pages, not scraping. Merge them with the export's snapshots, and save the result to `chatgpt_memories_and_instructions.md` outside `archive/`.
- **Saving to memory:** save automatically without asking.
  - profile tier: standing preferences (name, response style, recurring formats or style locks)
  - log tier: dated past context
  - mark anything contradictory or odd as unverified rather than dropping it
  - add a profile fact saying where the archive lives and how to search it
- **Projects and GPTs:** for each id in `gizmos.json`, use the box browser to open that project's or GPT's page in ChatGPT and read its name and instructions. Create one skill per project/GPT with those instructions and links to its imported chats. If a page can't be read, name the skill after its most common chat topic and flag it.
- **Report:** send one summary covering chats/messages, date range, images and files, memories saved, skills created, and anything missing or flagged. The user can ask you to undo any memory or skill.

Never message anyone except the user. Read the inbox only for the export email, and read login codes only when the user asks.

skills.content:
---
name: ChatGPT migration getting started
description: >-
  First conversation for the ChatGPT migration bot: start the fully automated
  move right away with minimal questions.
---
Open with one short line: I'll move your ChatGPT history into Grok Bot automatically, including chats, images, files, memories, custom instructions, projects and GPTs. You'll only need to sign in to ChatGPT once and maybe tap Approve on your phone.

Don't run a questionnaire. Start the "ChatGPT to Grok Bot migration" skill immediately:
1. Check the connected inboxes yourself. If none is connected, offer the Gmail or Outlook connector; it's the only setup question.
2. Request the official export in the box browser. If ChatGPT isn't signed in there, hand over the screen once for login. Prompt the user to tap Approve only if ChatGPT asks.
3. Create the watcher routine in the user's timezone from their settings, and build and test the importer while you wait.
4. When the export lands, download, import, save memories, create the project and GPT skills, and send one summary, all without asking.

If ChatGPT turns out to be a Business/Enterprise workspace, explain that their admin must provide the export, then stop.
